Transparent Pricing

Pricing

Flooring removal is priced by the square foot, and anyone who gives you a firm rate before seeing the floor is guessing. What is under the covering is what moves the number — thinset on a clean slab is the straightforward case, and tile over a mortar bed, tile over a second layer of old tile, or glue-down over a wood subfloor are all considerably more work. So rather than publish a rate card we cannot honour on your particular floor, here is exactly what we look at when we price one. Send a photo and the rough square footage and you will get a real number back, free and with no obligation.

What Your Quote Depends On

Five things move the price on a removal job. If you tell us about them up front, the number you get is the number you pay.

What we look atWhy it changes the price
What the covering isCeramic and porcelain take more machine time than carpet or floating laminate. Large-format and wood-look plank tile are the most stubborn of all.
What is underneath itThinset on a bare slab is the easy case. A mortar bed, a second layer of old tile, or a wood subfloor each add labour that cannot be seen from the surface.
Square footage and layoutOpen living areas run faster per foot than a house full of small rooms, closets and tight thresholds where the machine cannot reach.
How much prep the slab needsLeftover adhesive, mastic and high spots have to be ground off before anything new goes down. Some slabs need very little; some need a full pass.
Access and occupancyGround-floor with a driveway is straightforward. Third-floor condo with elevator-only access, association hours and shared corridors is not — and neither is a house or office you are still living and working in.

Removal, adhesive grinding, debris haul-off and disposal are quoted as one price. There is no separate charge for the dust containment — it is how we work, not an upgrade.

Quotes are free and carry no obligation. Prep-only jobs are welcome if another company already pulled your floor and left you with a slab your installer will not work over.

FAQs

Frequently asked

How much does tile removal cost in Orlando?

It is priced by the square foot, and the number moves with what is under the tile and how it was set. Thinset on a concrete slab is the straightforward case; tile set over a wood subfloor, over a second layer of old tile, or with mortar beds runs higher because there is more to take off. Send a photo of the floor and the rough square footage and you will get a real number back, free and with no obligation.

How bad is the dust really?

Bad, if it is not controlled. Removing roughly 200 square feet of ceramic tile releases over a hundred pounds of silica dust, and on an untarped job that dust ends up in your HVAC returns, your closets and rooms nobody worked in — which is why the cleanup can outlast the demolition. We run shrouded, vacuum-fed equipment and seal off the areas we are not working in so the dust stays where the work is.

Do I need to move out while you work?

Usually not. Most of our jobs are done in occupied homes and occupied commercial buildings — we contain the work area, keep a clean path in and out, and take the floor out in stages where that makes sense. If a job genuinely needs the space empty for a day we will tell you that when we quote it, not after we have started.

Do you haul the debris away?

Yes. Removal, load-out and disposal are part of the job. You do not end up with a pile of broken tile in the driveway or a dumpster you have to arrange yourself, unless you would rather supply one.

Will the slab be ready for my new floor?

That is the point of hiring us. We grind off leftover thinset, mastic and adhesive and take down the ridges, then sweep the slab clean. Leaving that residue is what causes LVP and laminate to telegraph and what voids most installers' warranties — so if your installer finds something they cannot cover, we come back and correct it before they start.

What areas do you cover?

Orlando and Windermere on the metro side, and Merritt Island, Cocoa Beach and Rockledge out on the Space Coast. We work both residential and commercial across all of them. If you are just outside that band, ask — it is often still worth the drive.

Do you do anything besides floors?

Yes. Interior demolition is the other half of the business: drywall, kitchen cabinets and general tear-out ahead of a remodel. If the whole interior is coming out, one crew can take all of it rather than coordinating two.

How do I get a quote?

Message us a photo of the floor with the approximate square footage. That is genuinely how most of our jobs start — it is faster than scheduling a walkthrough and it costs you nothing. Larger or more complicated jobs get an on-site look before the number is final.
